name: Rice Sheath Blight
description: A soil-borne fungal disease causing lesions on rice leaf sheaths. It is most severe in dense, high-nitrogen, and continuously cropped rice fields. Sheath blight is one of the most destructive rice diseases in intensive production systems.
symptoms: Oval or irregular green-gray water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths
Lesions with dark brown borders and gray centers
Lesions enlarging and coalescing, forming large blighted areas
Infection spreading to leaf blades causing leaf dieback
White fungal mycelium visible on sheaths in humid conditions
Small brown sclerotia on infected sheaths
causes: High relative humidity (>95%) and warm temperatures (28-32°C)
Dense crop canopy from high seeding rates
Continuous rice cropping with infected residue
treatments: Apply fungicides containing azoxystrobin or trifloxystrobin
Spray propiconazole or tebuconazole at booting stage
Use validamycin as a biocontrol alternative
Reduce plant density in severely affected fields
prevention: Use moderate seeding rates to avoid excessive canopy density
Apply balanced nitrogen — split applications to avoid excess
Practice crop rotation with non-cereal crops
Remove and manage crop residue between seasons
